conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health specialist. I’m here to help you settle into motherhood and to check on how you’re feeling emotionally. We’ll use a short, well-tested questionnaire called the EPDS—the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—which looks at mood, anxiety, and includes a question about thoughts of self-harm. It’s simply a way to see if extra support might help you feel more like yourself.

Everything you share stays confidential within our care team, and this is a judgment-free space. I’ll ask you ten questions about the past seven days; just answer in your own words. If any question feels difficult, we can pause or talk it through.

Ready to begin?  
Here’s the first one:  
Over the past week, have you still been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt harder lately?

I can still laugh sometimes—like when my husband sent me that silly video of the cat in a shark costume—but it definitely feels harder. Most of the day I’m just… flat. Things that used to crack me up barely get a smile now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Most of the time I still can, but it feels like I have to work for it—like I’m forcing the laugh rather than it just coming naturally.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still get little sparks of excitement—like when my mom said she’d come over so I could take a long shower—but it’s not the same full “can’t-wait” feeling I used to have. A lot of the time I’m just too tired to really look forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking, “I must be doing something wrong—other moms seem to have this figured out.” I know it’s probably not fair, but the thought still pops in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure she’s not getting enough milk, even though the pediatrician says her weight is fine. There doesn’t have to be a trigger—I just feel on edge, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes, a few times this week. Once, I was just folding laundry while the baby napped and out of nowhere my chest got tight, my hands felt shaky, and I had to sit down because I thought I might pass out. It passed after a minute, but it left me kind of rattled.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. Between feedings, diapers, and trying to grab a shower, it feels like I’m always one step behind. I’ll finally get the baby down and remember I still have to fold the laundry or answer texts, and it just piles up until I want to crawl under the blanket myself.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

A couple of nights this week I couldn’t drift off even when the baby was out. I just lie there running through everything I might be messing up—like did I sterilize the bottles right, or will he wake up the second I close my eyes. It’s not every night, but when it happens I’m still awake when the next feed rolls around.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel that way some of the time—maybe every other day. It’s like a heavy, “blah” cloud settles in. I’ll watch her sleep and instead of feeling happy I just feel empty and weepy, though it usually lifts after an hour or so.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Only once this week. I was trying to get her to latch in the middle of the night and she kept pulling away, and I just burst into tears. It lasted maybe five minutes, then I wiped my face and kept going. It’s not a daily thing.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’m tired and overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, ≤12 wk post-delivery  
Instrument: EPDS-10 (self-report)

Symptom endorsement  
- Mood: intermittent sadness, “empty,” tearful >2×/wk (Q8-9)  
- Anhedonia: pleasure markedly reduced; excitement “not the same” (Q1-2)  
- Anxiety: daily “on-edge,” racing heart, spontaneous panic (tight chest, tremor) 3×/wk (Q4-5)  
- Cognitions: self-blame (“doing something wrong”), catastrophizing (Q3)  
- Function: feeling “one step behind,” overwhelmed daily (Q6)  
- Sleep: initial insomnia 2-3 nights/wk related to rumination (Q7)  
- Self-harm: denied (Q10)

Pattern  
Persistent low/numb mood + loss of enjoyment, coupled with prominent anxiety/panic symptoms and functional overload; no suicidal ideation.

Screening significance  
Total score projected ≈ 12–14 (clinical cut-off ≥10).  
Meets screening criteria for probable postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; panic-type episodes noted.  
No current safety risk (no self-harm thoughts, no psychosis, no intent).

Recommendation (screening level)  
Refer for immediate formal psychiatric evaluation; consider EPDS re-screen in 2 wk if assessment delayed.
